title: The pre-eruption state of T CrB as observed with ALMA in 2024
question: What is the pre-eruption state of T CrB and what are the properties (density, temperature, ionization) of the circumstellar medium and red giant wind into which the imminent nova ejecta will expand?

data.arrays: 12 m main array (41-44 antennas) and 7 m ACA array (9-10 antennas, test only)
data.angular_resolution: 0.303x0.184 arcsec to 8.14x5.68 arcsec (12m array); 0.48x0.35 arcsec (Bands 7+8 combined)
data.sensitivity: 17 to 114 uJy/beam continuum RMS (12m array per-MOUS); 0.018 mJy/beam (all 12m combined); 0.16 to 8.2 mJy/beam per channel

what.value: VLA 5 GHz to 35 GHz flux density spectra of T CrB in 2016/17

evidence.loc: Spectral re-analysis of the 2016/17 VLA data
evidence.quote: We can, however, assume a smooth spectral transition to the frequency window just below ours and compare to the measurements made by L2019 in 2016/17 with the VLA at 5 GHz to 35 GHz.

what.value: Gaia DR3 distance to T CrB (D ~ 895 pc)

evidence.quote: Now, we use equation [\[eq:K\]](#eq:K) to obtain a relation between $n_0$, $R$ and $T_0$, knowing $\beta$ and using the distance $D\sim$895 pc (cite: 2021AJ....161..147B).

what.value: Gaia EDR3 proper motion and astrometry for T CrB

evidence.loc: Calibration, imaging, and flux density measurements
evidence.quote: The T CrB position used was (ICRS) RA 15:59:30.154, DEC +25.55.12.909 (Epoch 2025-08-10, 22:40:20.4 UT), with proper motion in RA = -6.853E-16 rad/s, in DEC = 1.846E-15 rad/s in agreement with the values from (cite: gaia_edr3).

what.value: Orbital parameters, distance, inclination, and stellar masses/radii of T CrB

evidence.quote: Independent of the particular value of the distance considered, the binary orbit is found to be circular to a high precision with period of 227.55 days.
(the inclination of the system is between $49^\circ$ and $56^\circ$ according to the latest analysis by (cite: 2025ApJ...983...76H)).

what.value: Orbital phase ephemeris of T CrB

evidence.quote: The orbital phase is computed from the centroid JD following (cite: 2000AJ....119.1375F).

recipe.goal: Search for spectral line emission and derive line upper limits
recipe.method: Per-day, per-SPW continuum-subtracted full spectral resolution cubes were searched using the ALMA QA Pipeline line search algorithm and visual inspection; a 2-sigma upper limit on HCN v=0 J=4-3 in combined Band 7+7b SPW 4 was derived from the peak channel.
key_parameters: velocity resolution 0.82 km/s in Band 7 SPW 4
assumptions: 10 km/s line width assumed for the HCN J=4-3 upper limit

recipe.goal: Measure per-band/per-visit continuum flux densities and noise RMS
recipe.method: Image each 12m MOUS over aggregate bandwidth with CASA tclean (mtmfs, robust=0.5), estimate RMS in an annulus between 30% and 60% of the primary beam radius in the non-PB-corrected image, and fit a 2D Gaussian to an elliptical region of synthesized beam size around the peak to take the peak of the fitted Gaussian as flux density.
key_parameters: deconvolver='mtmfs' (nterms=2 where fractional bandwidth > 10%), Briggs robust=0.5, pixel width = 10% of synthesized beam minor axis
assumptions: Source is an unresolved point source; systematic absolute flux calibration uncertainty is 2.5% in Bands 1-5 and 5% in Bands 6-8

recipe.goal: Fit power-law SED to ALMA continuum flux densities and cross-check with combined MTMFS imaging
recipe.method: Fit power law F(nu) = F0 * nu^alpha to the five concurrent phase 0.43 points and to all nine points using scipy.optimize.curve_fit in Python 3; cross-check by imaging all 12m data combined with tclean MTMFS (nterms=2) and reading the central pixel of the PB-corrected alpha and alpha.error images.
key_parameters: Power law F(nu) = F0 * nu^alpha with nu in GHz; tclean MTMFS with nterms=2
assumptions: Power-law spectral energy distribution across 42 to 400 GHz

recipe.goal: Constrain extended continuum emission and circum-binary brightness temperature
recipe.method: Combine all Band 7 and 8 data to maximize angular resolution and measure the mean surface brightness and RMS in an annulus of inner radius 0.8 arcsec and outer radius 1.6 arcsec centered on T CrB to derive a 2-sigma continuum surface brightness and brightness temperature upper limit.
key_parameters: Annulus inner radius = 0.8 arcsec, outer radius = 1.6 arcsec; beam FWHM = 0.48 x 0.35 arcsec; confidence level = 2 sigma
assumptions: Gaia DR3 distance of ~895 pc used to convert 0.8-1.6 arcsec to 720-1440 AU

recipe.goal: Re-analyze 2016/17 VLA high-state spectra from Linford et al. (2019)
recipe.method: Fit separate power laws to the upper four frequency points (13.5 GHz to 35 GHz) of the seven per-visit VLA spectra from Linford et al. (2019), excluding two nights affected by atmospheric delay model and decorrelation systematics, and compare the resulting spectral indices with the 2024 ALMA index.
key_parameters: Frequency range 13.5 GHz to 35 GHz (4 data points per night across 5 retained nights)
assumptions: Smooth spectral transition between the upper VLA band (13.5-35 GHz) and the ALMA frequency range (42-407 GHz)

recipe.goal: Model stellar wind density profile, temperature, density scale, and mass-loss rate
recipe.method: Apply an analytical isotropic, isothermal, fully ionized free-free stellar wind model in the hybrid optical depth regime: solve Eq. 2 for the wind density exponent beta from alpha, set lower limits on turnover frequency nu_t from the highest observed frequencies, and use Eqs. 3 and 6 to constrain the allowed (n0, T0) parameter space and mass-loss rate for candidate donor radii R.
assumptions: Isotropic, isothermal (T0 > 10^4 K), fully ionized wind with power-law density n(r) = n0 (r/R)^(-beta); Rayleigh-Jeans approximation (h*nu << k_B*T0); distance D ~ 895 pc; wind launch velocity = 10 km/s
